author: CNN
description:
Both Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas and Israeli Prime Minister addressed the UN General Assembly Thursday.

Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas addressed the UN via video after again being denied an entry visa by the Trump administration. He called on global leaders to hold Israel accountable and for the implementation of the stalled 20-point Gaza ceasefire plan.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu lambasted Tehran, dramatically claiming that if he hadn’t attacked Iran, “we’d all be dead.” He also defended Israel's war in Gaza. Netanyahu provoked a polarized reaction as he took to the podium, and a large number of diplomats walked out of the room. Others stood and applauded the Israeli leader. “If there are any other moral cowards who haven’t yet left this hall, please do so now,” Netanyahu said.

0:00 Recapping Netanyahu's UN speech, denying genocide
2:40 Palestinian Authority President's UN speech
4:31 Palestinian MP Mustafa Barghouti reacts to Netany
title: '2 different versions of reality': Unpacking Israel & Palestine UN speeches

description:
Speaking to reporters in a New York hotel after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addressed the United Nations, Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran had presented a proposal to the US that — according to Iran — would re-open the Strait of Hormuz and restart negotiations toward a “final deal.”

The proposal, presented to the US through mediators this week, calls for the US to meet certain conditions within seven days to restart the talks and re-open the strait, Araghchi said.

In response to Araghchi’s comments, a White House official told CNN they were having “positive and constructive discussions through the mediators.”

The country craves economic relief. People think groceries and the roofs over their heads are too expensive. description:
Satellite imagery and intelligence support provided by Chinese groups have helped Iran threaten ships in the Strait of Hormuz and launch precision strikes on US military bases in the Middle East, part of a dramatic improvement in Iranian targeting capabilities over the past several months, according to a series of recent American intelligence assessments described to CNN by four sources.

The imagery allowed Iran to strike a US base in Jordan in July, a strike that killed three American service members, with a level of precision US officials believe was otherwise beyond Iran’s capabilities, the sources said.

US officials say that it’s difficult to precisely quantify the scope of China’s assistance, in part because it’s not clear whether the Chinese government has ordered it or is merely tacitly allowing the support, and some officials disagree about how much Beijing is helping. title: Intel from China helped Iran target US troops: Sources

description:
An early fall nor’easter is gathering strength along the central East Coast, pounding beaches in several states with heavy surf and threatening to bring coastal flooding, wind and rain to parts of the Northeast through the weekend. 

The nor’easter, named for the direction its punishing winds come from, currently sits several hundred miles off the Mid-Atlantic coast and will begin to track north and strengthen over the next two days. More than 40 million people will feel the impacts from the nor’easter from now through the weekend, from either wind, rain, coastal flooding or some combination of those. 

CNN meteorologist Allison Chinchar says the slow-moving storm is set to bring "round after round" of strong winds and heavy rain to coastal communities. Also, News 12 New Jersey's Lauren Due reports conditions from a New Jersey beach and Chief Michael Cranson of the Nantucket Fire Department says he expects flooding.

Eight US Navy personnel assigned to the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group attempted suicide during a period that included when the ships undertook combat operations against Iran and the carrier set a modern record for its time at sea, according to a letter from the service’s acting secretary, which was obtained by CNN.

Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao revealed the number, which has not been previously reported and covers crew members from several ships that travel together, including the carrier, in written responses to questions posed by Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand about the morale and mental health of the USS Abraham Lincoln’s crew. Cao wrote that no service members had killed themselves during the deployment.
